title: Fluxborne Act Expansion Sprint
specification:
# Fluxborne Act Expansion Sprint

This PRD is intentionally lane-pure. PM should decompose it into a large Fluxborne-only sprint for `action-agent`.

## Product Goal

Push Fluxborne forward as the largest action project in the repo with a more substantial act-scale loop: stronger combat progression, clearer contract / mission structure, richer home base payoff, and better continuity between combat runs and long-term advancement.

The player experience should move toward:

- more meaningful combat build decisions
- clearer mission or contract goals
- stronger home base utility
- better continuity across acts, waves, maps, and upgrades

## Sprint Shape

Expected shape:

- 12 to 18 implementation tasks
- all tasks assigned to `action-agent`
- one shared action lane branch
- one Fluxborne PR with many commits
- no cross-lane work

This is intentionally the largest of the three PRDs.

## Scope Boundaries

Stay inside:

- `src/barebones-starter/games/apps/fluxborne/**`

Primary areas likely to matter:

- `config.ts`
- `components/**`
- `game/combat/**`
- `game/player/**`
- `game/map/**`
- `game/progression/**`
- `game/homeBase/**`
- `game/workshop/**`
- `game/story/**`
- `game/endless/**`
- `game/npc/**`
- `types.ts`

## Deliverable Themes

PM should spread the task plan across most of these areas.

### 1. Combat and Build Depth

- deepen player build choices, weapon identity, or combat role specialization
- strengthen the connection between moment-to-moment combat and longer-term loadout strategy
- improve combat readability where complexity increases

### 2. Contract / Mission Structure

- strengthen the player’s sense of run objectives
- add or improve mission board, contract cadence, or reward loops
- make run goals more deliberate than pure survival drift

### 3. Map and Progression Continuity

- improve transitions between zones, acts, or wave phases
- make exploration, unlocks, and progression systems feel connected
- reinforce the sense of advancing through a larger campaign loop

### 4. Home Base and Service Value

- make home base rooms and services more strategically meaningful
- improve the payoff of returning from a run
- connect services to combat progression, loadouts, or contracts

### 5. NPC / Story / World Feedback

- improve story-state visibility, NPC utility, or relationship affordances
- make progression beats feel acknowledged in the world
- strengthen player understanding of what changed after key milestones

### 6. Presentation and Interface Readability

- improve clarity in heavy-system screens such as contracts, maps, inventory, stats, or home base views
- reduce confusion around progression and player choice

## Planning Rules For PM

- Do not emit tasks for other agents.
- Do not emit reviewer tasks.
- Prefer substantial system work over documentation-only or note-only tasks.
- Use existing Fluxborne systems and directories as the basis for decomposition.
- Make the task list large enough that the resulting PR legitimately contains many commits.
- Include tests where the touched Fluxborne subsystem already has useful test coverage patterns.

## Definition Of Done

- Fluxborne gains a noticeably larger act-scale loop.
- Combat, contracts, map progression, and home base all feel more connected.
- The sprint spans multiple major Fluxborne subsystems rather than one isolated feature slice.
- The final lane PR should plausibly contain many commits because the PM decomposition is intentionally large.

## Explicit Non-Goals

- no changes outside Fluxborne scope
- no filler tasks created only to drive up commit count
- no PM-generated reviewer work
requirements: Produce between 12 and 18 implementation tasks total.
Assign every implementation task to action-agent only.
Do not create tasks for aquarium-agent
Keep every task scoped to files under src/barebones-starter/games/apps/fluxborne/ only.
Tasks must be atomic enough to land as one commit each on the shared action lane branch.
The resulting implementation should feel like one large Fluxborne sprint rather than isolated note files.
The reviewer should merge one action PR after the lane finishes all tasks.

tasks.title: Create act-aware contract board model and persistence
tasks.description: Add a persisted contract-board domain for Fluxborne that can generate deterministic board entries, track one active contract, accumulate progress, and resolve rewards across acts, zones, waves, and campaign milestones.
acceptance: Save/load can round-trip a contract board plus one active contract without breaking older Fluxborne saves.
Pure helpers can generate, accept, progress, complete, and claim contracts for at least kill, XP, wave, zone, exploration, and act-frontier objective types.
Node tests cover normalization, board refresh cadence, progress delta calculation, and reward-claim resolution.

tasks.title: Surface the contract board in home base
tasks.description: Expose the new contract board in home base so returning from a run gives the player a clear accept, continue, and claim loop instead of opaque progression drift.
acceptance: Home base renders available contracts, the current active contract, claimable rewards, and refresh timing or cadence messaging.
Accepting or claiming a contract updates the relevant refs and persists through the existing save path.
Locked, empty, active, and claim-ready states each render distinct copy and controls so the player can tell what to do next.

tasks.title: Add an in-run mission tracker HUD
tasks.description: Show the player exactly what the current contract requires during combat and transitions by adding a live objective tracker and completion-ready messaging to the existing HUD surfaces.
acceptance: The HUD shows active contract title, metric progress, and completion-ready state when a contract is active and stays hidden when none is active.
Wave or zone transition messaging can announce newly completed contract steps without obscuring existing combat readability.
The tracker supports at least kill, XP, zone, and wave style contracts using live runtime state rather than hardcoded UI values.

tasks.title: Extend act progression into campaign frontier metadata
tasks.description: Upgrade story progression from raw milestone flags into reusable frontier metadata that can describe the current campaign phase, next milestone, and return-to-base guidance across the sprint.
acceptance: Story helpers can resolve a current frontier and next milestone from persisted act state without duplicating switch logic in UI or map code.
Existing story tests expand to cover frontier resolution across act1, act2, act3, and completed milestone chains.
If any new persisted frontier metadata is added, save/load keeps it stable for existing Fluxborne save files.

tasks.title: Show campaign continuity in map views
tasks.description: Make map screens communicate where the campaign is going by surfacing zone completion, gated exits, frontier targets, and contract-relevant destinations in the minimap and full map viewer.
acceptance: The full map shows zone completion and highlights frontier or contract-relevant exits or zones when data is available.
The minimap uses distinct visuals for locked gates, required progression targets, and optional contract markers.
Map helper tests cover marker precedence for overlapping cases such as gated exits that are also contract targets.

tasks.title: Wire live gameplay events into contracts and frontier progress
tasks.description: Connect kills, wave clears, zone transitions, and exploration milestones to the new contract and campaign-frontier systems so progression advances from actual play instead of manual bookkeeping.
acceptance: Kill-, wave-, zone-, and exploration-based contracts all progress from live gameplay events and not from UI-only triggers.
Story-mode and endless-mode wave sources feed the same contract progression helpers when relevant.
Tests cover at least one kill-based, one wave-based, and one zone or exploration-based contract progression scenario with persistence-safe outputs.

tasks.title: Implement skill path selection and respec flow
tasks.description: Turn the existing skill-path contract layer into a real player-facing choice and respec loop tied to Fluxborne UI and Voss-driven interactions.
acceptance: The player can choose a skill path from a real UI flow once the path-choice gate is met, and the selected path persists through save/load.
A respec flow is exposed through the Voss interaction path, applies shard and day costs through the existing rules, and updates respec tracking without breaking current passive or ability behavior.
Skill-path tests cover first-choice gating, invalid selection normalization, and respec success and failure cases.

tasks.title: Improve build summary and preset compatibility UI
tasks.description: Make build-heavy screens easier to reason about by showing path identity, archetype focus, and preset compatibility directly in the existing Inventory and Stats flows.
acceptance: Inventory or Stats shows selected path, key passive identity, archetype focus, and active preset status in one readable summary.
Saving or applying a preset surfaces compatibility warnings when the current path or loadout diverges from the preset's intended build.
Retention or save tests are updated if preset metadata or serialization changes.

tasks.title: Deepen ranged weapon specialization and mastery
tasks.description: Strengthen combat build decisions by giving Fluxborne's gun archetypes clearer identity and mastery hooks that materially change how each loadout plays.
acceptance: At least three ranged archetypes gain distinct combat behavior or mastery payoff beyond raw stat tuning.
The new identity is implemented in player and weapon logic, not only in descriptive copy or UI labels.
game/player tests cover each new archetype rule or mastery trigger that changes live combat behavior.

tasks.title: Add combat readability for build-state timers and procs
tasks.description: Expose the temporary states that now matter to Fluxborne builds by extending feedback and HUD systems for execution windows, mastery timers, proc states, and similar combat signals.
acceptance: The HUD or combat feedback layers surface at least three build-state timers or proc cues such as execution, flux mastery, finisher window, or gun-class proc state.
The added cues remain readable alongside the existing HP, Flux, Surge, and weapon HUD elements.
Combat runtime or related pure tests cover any new feedback-resolution or timer-helper logic.

tasks.title: Implement armory favorites and quick-equip actions
tasks.description: Complete the deferred armory depth by adding favorite management and quick-equip operations that connect melee gear, ranged loadouts, and saved build priorities.
acceptance: Armory service can persist favorite gear state and return favorite metadata from equipment snapshots.
Armory UI lets the player mark favorites and quick-equip favored or preset-linked gear without desyncing ranged and melee equipment state.
Armory service tests cover favorite toggle persistence plus quick-equip success and failure cases.

tasks.title: Implement workshop reforge and progression-gated unlocks
tasks.description: Turn workshop reforge from a stub into a strategic service and connect workshop unlocks to real progression beats such as act milestones or contract rewards.
acceptance: Workshop service implements reforge with concrete shard costs, deterministic output handling, and persistence wiring.
Recipe or upgrade availability can unlock from long-form progression state such as act milestones or contract claims instead of staying static-only.
Workshop or home-base tests cover reforge outcomes, unlock gating, and completed-job collection after unlock changes.

tasks.title: Implement training dummy modes and local leaderboards
tasks.description: Replace the current training-room placeholders with real dummy mode launching, richer result tracking, and local leaderboard presentation that feeds back into build planning.
acceptance: Training room exposes dummy session modes and per-course leaderboard or best-result views instead of placeholder text.
Training service records best results deterministically across repeated runs and shapes leaderboard data for UI consumption.
Home-base tests cover dummy start hooks, leaderboard output, and best-result persistence.

tasks.title: Implement medical stat upgrades and post-run planning cues
tasks.description: Make the medical bay more strategically valuable by supporting stat-point spending and clearer recovery or planning guidance after the player returns from a run.
acceptance: Medical service implements stat-point spending with validation, updated save slices, and persistence behavior.
Medical bay or the hub presents actionable recovery or planning cues such as available stat upgrades, pending cure issues, or next-step build hints.
Medical service tests cover stat-upgrade success, insufficient-point failure, and persisted results.

tasks.title: Expand NPC and world feedback for contracts and milestones
tasks.description: Make Fluxborne's world acknowledge the larger act loop by adding new service-NPC and Voss reactions to contract state, home-base growth, act frontiers, and reputation milestones.
acceptance: At least Voss and one service NPC gain dialog or affordance changes that react to contract state, act frontier progression, or home-base growth.
Relevant dialog effects can update dialog flags, affinity, or reputation through the existing effect plumbing without breaking current quest flows.
NPC or story tests cover trigger evaluation, priority, or stateful reaction cases added for the new milestone-aware feedback.

tasks.title: Bridge endless milestones into home-base continuity
tasks.description: Connect Fluxborne's endless progression back into the main campaign payoff loop by surfacing best-wave and milestone data in home base instead of leaving it isolated.
acceptance: Endless progression exposes next milestone goal or reward data and home base surfaces current best-wave continuity to the player.
Trophy hall or the home-base hub shows endless milestone progress alongside act or home-base progress so side-mode advancement feels connected.
Existing endless tests expand to cover milestone mapping or persistence behavior for the new home-base-facing summary data.
